meta.title: Egypt vs Iran — 2026 World Cup, Group G decider
meta.kickoffStatus: pre-match (confirmed XIs + shirt numbers drop ~1hr before kickoff)
meta.verificationNote: Spine fact-checked against Wikipedia/ESPN/Al Jazeera/FOX/Opta. Player clubs/values from Transfermarkt June 2026. Shirt numbers are from the official 2026 World Cup squad list (Wikipedia). Tactics/lineups are projected from current squads, not a confirmed teamsheet.
knownCorrections: Marmoush had a QUIET 2025-26 at Man City (~3 PL goals) — the draft's '27-goal season' is false (that was Frankfurt 2024-25).
Taremi ~58 goals / ~103 caps pre-WC, now at Olympiacos (not Inter, not 60/104).
Ramy Rabia is at Al Ain (UAE), not Al Ahly. Hamdy Fathy at Al-Wakrah (Qatar) and a MATCH DOUBT. Ibrahim Adel at Nordsjælland.
Jahanbakhsh at FCV Dender (Belgium); Ghoddos at Kalba (UAE); Ezatolahi at Shabab Al-Ahli (UAE).
Sardar Azmoun is NOT in Iran's 2026 squad (political omission) — notable absence, not a player to watch.
Egypt's most-capped player is Ahmed Hassan (184); Hossam Hassan holds the SCORING record (69). Salah is on 68 — one shy of his own coach's all-time tally (already Egypt's all-time WC-finals scorer).
Hajsafi on ~148 caps — playing tonight EQUALS Nekounam's 149 record (count is live).
Iran does NOT lead Asia in WC appearances (South Korea, 12, does). Iran on its 7th.
Lumen Field is a FORMER loudest-stadium record holder (137.6 dB vs Saints 2013; Arrowhead now leads at 142.2).

referee.name: Szymon Marciniak (Poland)
referee.note: IFFHS World's Best Referee 2022 & 2023. Did the 2022 WC final AND 2023 UCL final. ~4 yellows/match — a let-it-flow game-manager. A final-caliber ref on a group game signals FIFA sees this as a high-stakes fixture.

weather.summary: Open pitch (Lumen's roof covers ~70% of seats, NOT the field).
weather.rain: 30-40% chance of showers, slim thunderstorm chance
weather.effect: Possibly damp/skiddy surface + gusty wind → nudges toward faster, more direct, set-piece-influenced play.

match.parallelMatch: New Zealand vs Belgium (Vancouver) kicks off simultaneously.

group.name: Group G
group.upsideDown: Belgium, the group heavyweight, sit 3rd after two draws and must beat NZ to be sure of advancing.

stakes.egypt: Win = group winners + first-ever knockout berth. Draw = guaranteed top-2 (advances), full stop — the only 'unless Belgium win by 3+' caveat decides 1st vs 2nd place/seeding, NOT survival. Lose = need to scoreboard-watch Vancouver.
stakes.iran: Win = essentially through (~5 pts), tops group if Belgium don't win. Draw = 3 pts but likely not enough; relies on best-third math (8 of 12 thirds advance) + the NZ-Belgium result. Lose = out.
stakes.fanShortcut: Egypt fans only need to glance at Vancouver if Iran are winning in Seattle. Iran fans: win and you're in.
stakes.opta: Egypt 44.1% win · Draw 31.3% · Iran 24.6% (25k sims). Egypt ~61% to top Group G.

headToHead.summary: First-ever COMPETITIVE meeting. Only ~2 prior, both friendlies — Iran 2-1 (1975), 1-1 draw (2000 LG Cup, Egypt won shootout). Egypt has never beaten Iran in regulation.
headToHead.biggerPicture: Neither nation has EVER reached a World Cup knockout round. Whoever advances tonight makes history.

egypt.nicknameOrigin: After ancient Egypt's rulers — heritage, power, dynasty.

coach.name: Hossam Hassan
coach.note: Egypt's all-time record SCORER (69 goals). The record Salah is chasing belongs to his own manager. Identical twin Ibrahim Hassan also a famous Egypt international. Appointed Feb 2024.

tactical.identity: Attack-minded but defensively excellent (~0.2 goals conceded/game in qualifying). Quick transition into 1v1s for the stars, not patient possession.
tactical.inPossession: Two holders (Attia + a partner) screen; Salah inverts from the right, Marmoush runs the channels as a mobile No. 9.
tactical.vulnerability: A packed low block (exactly Iran's offer) blunts the fast-break game; advanced full-backs leave space behind.

egypt.honours: Record 7 AFCON titles (incl. only-ever three-in-a-row 2006-08-10). EFA founded 1921, joined FIFA 1923 as first African + Arab member. 4th World Cup (1934 — first Arab/African team ever; 1990, 2018, 2026).

xi.name: Mohamed El Shenawy
xi.blurb: 37, four-time African champion, 2018 WC vet famed for big knockout saves. (Shobeir, 26, is the heir if rotated.)

xi.name: Mohamed Hany
xi.blurb: One-club Al Ahly lifer — academy to serial winner.

xi.name: Yasser Ibrahim
xi.blurb: One-club loyalist; scored his maiden international goal at 33.

xi.name: Ramy Rabia
xi.blurb: Once a teen prodigy chased by Man Utd & Dortmund; senior debut at 17, two CAF Champions Leagues. (Steps in if Hamdy Fathy fails fitness.)

xi.name: Ahmed Fatouh
xi.blurb: Egypt's overlapping engine; started both June group games. (Editorial: 2024 fatal DUI accident, suspended sentence — handle with care.)

xi.name: Marwan Attia
xi.blurb: Al Ahly's unglamorous engine-room — breaks play up, recycles.

xi.name: Mohanad Lasheen
xi.blurb: Won 2024-25 CAF Champions League with Pyramids — tournament-tested.

xi.name: Zizo (Ahmed Sayed)
xi.blurb: Cairo-derby crossover star — defected Zamalek→Al Ahly on a free, one of the league's most controversial moves. NOT the Nantes striker Mostafa Mohamed.

xi.name: Mohamed Salah
xi.blurb: The main event. One goal from equalling coach Hossam Hassan's 69-goal national record. Likely his last World Cup; leaving Liverpool this summer. Already Egypt's all-time WC-finals scorer.

xi.name: Emam Ashour
xi.blurb: Egypt's chief line-breaker; scored vs Belgium. Back from a 2025 of shoulder injury + hepatitis A. (Draft's 'heart issue' is unverified.)

xi.name: Omar Marmoush
xi.blurb: Dream City move off a sensational Frankfurt 2024-25, but year one in Manchester has been quiet (~3 PL goals). The WC is his chance to rediscover the edge alongside Salah.

bench.name: Trézéguet
bench.note: Inverted winger, 2nd World Cup, arrives at the back post

bench.name: Ibrahim Adel
bench.note: Pacey young wide threat, CAF CL winner with Pyramids

egypt.doubts: Hamdy Fathy (Al-Wakrah, doubt) & Hossam Abdelmaguid doubtful. Mostafa Mohamed (Nantes) reportedly LEFT OUT of the 26 (squad status disputed). Salah & Marmoush fit.

iran.nicknameOrigin: Persian 'Tim-e Melli' = literally 'the National Team'. Also 'Princes of Persia'.

coach.name: Amir Ghalenoei
coach.note: Second Iran spell (first 2006-08); most successful manager in Iranian league history (5 titles). Took Iran to 2023 Asian Cup semis. Switched to a 5-4-1 low block vs Belgium (0-0).

tactical.identity: Compact, disciplined, physical veteran block. Forces play wide, defends with positional savvy.
tactical.inPossession: Direct/long to Taremi as reference point; Ghoddos connects, Jahanbakhsh attacks wide space on the break.
tactical.vulnerability: Thin creativity vs a set defense; heavy reliance on Taremi — contain him and the threat thins.

iran.honours: 3 AFC Asian Cup titles (1968, 1972, 1976 — three straight; 50-year drought since). 7th World Cup (1978, 1998, 2006, 2014, 2018, 2022, 2026) — eliminated in the group stage at all 7, closest miss 2018 (out by a point).

xi.name: Alireza Beiranvand
xi.trait: The Wall of Persia with a cannon arm
xi.blurb: Shepherd's son who slept rough & washed cars before becoming Iran's No.1. SAVED RONALDO'S PENALTY (2018). Two Guinness throw/kick records. Just produced a 7-save MOTM shutout of Belgium.

xi.name: Ramin Rezaeian
xi.blurb: Scored AND assisted vs New Zealand — became the OLDEST Asian player ever to score at a World Cup. Egypt's left flank must track him.

xi.name: Hossein Kanaani
xi.blurb: Two-WC veteran; scored in the 14-0 Cambodia rout. Backed imprisoned footballer Amir Nasr-Azadani during the 2022 protests.

xi.name: Shoja Khalilzadeh
xi.trait: 37-year-old captain who tackles like an artist
xi.blurb: Late bloomer; just captained Tractor to its first-ever league title. Twice Asia's best CB. Would make his World Cup DEBUT at 37.

xi.name: Ali Nemati
xi.blurb: Built his name on Persepolis title teams; Iran's flexible defensive cover.

xi.name: Ehsan Hajsafi
xi.blurb: Captain across FOUR straight World Cups (2014-2026). On 148 caps — level with Ali Daei, one shy of Nekounam's all-time record. Every minute edges him toward history.

xi.name: Alireza Jahanbakhsh
xi.trait: Cuts inside, arrives late in the box
xi.blurb: Won the 2017-18 Eredivisie Golden Boot (21 goals, AZ) — first Asian EVER to top-score a major European league. Club-record Brighton move followed; titles & a Conference League final at Feyenoord. Frequent Iran captain.

xi.name: Saman Ghoddos
xi.blurb: Turned down Sweden for Iran. Creative engine of Östersunds' fairytale under a young Graham Potter — won 2-1 at Arsenal's Emirates in 2018. Four years at Brentford.

xi.name: Saeid Ezatolahi
xi.blurb: Former prodigy — once Iran's youngest-ever scorer (19). Globe-trotter: Atlético Madrid → Rostov → Reading → Dubai. Turned scorer in 2025-26 (5 club goals).

xi.name: Mohammad Mohebi
xi.trait: Tall inverted winger who cuts in & finishes
xi.blurb: 2 goals + 2 assists on debut vs Cambodia (2019). The WC is both a stage and a contract audition.

xi.name: Mehdi Taremi
xi.trait: Ice-cold poacher with the audacity to try the spectacular
xi.blurb: Iran's talisman & all-time top WC-finals scorer (brace vs England 2022). Made his name at Porto; bicycle kick at Chelsea = UEFA Goal of the Season. Reached the 2024-25 UCL final with Inter (2nd Iranian ever). Iran's penalty taker & focal point.

bench.name: Mehdi Ghayedi
bench.note: Highest squad MV (€4.5m); pocket-sized electric 1v1 winger

bench.name: Mahdi Torabi
bench.note: Tireless wide man; the face of Iran's visa ordeal

bench.name: Amirhossein Hosseinzadeh
bench.note: Converted poacher; 2024-25 Iran league top scorer — fresh attacking spark

iran.doubts: None reported — squad intact apart from Azmoun's omission.

notableAbsence.name: Sardar Azmoun
notableAbsence.note: The 'Iranian Messi', one of Iran's all-time top scorers, LEFT OUT of even the 30-man squad over a political dispute. The ghost at the feast.

watch.name: Mohamed Salah
watch.blurb: The main event. One goal from his own coach's all-time Egypt record (69). Almost certainly his last World Cup.

watch.name: Mehdi Taremi
watch.blurb: Iran live or die by his finishing. ~58 goals, brace vs England in 2022, a UCL finalist in 2025.

watch.name: Omar Marmoush
watch.blurb: Pace and two-footed finishing — the reason Salah can drift central. Out to rediscover his Frankfurt form.

watch.name: Alireza Beiranvand
watch.blurb: Folk hero — slept rough as a teen, saved a Ronaldo penalty in 2018, 7 saves vs Belgium. Can steal a tight game alone.

watch.name: Alireza Jahanbakhsh
watch.blurb: First Asian to win a European league golden boot (Eredivisie 2017-18). Iran's calm head and wide threat.

watch.name: Emam Ashour
watch.blurb: Egypt's box-to-box connector and Salah's most willing runner. Scored vs Belgium.

keyBattles.title: Salah vs Iran's left side
keyBattles.blurb: Cutting in off the right, Salah meets a double-team in the low block. Watch if he drifts central to combine with Marmoush rather than forcing the 1v1 — and if RB Hany gets overlap space when Iran narrow.

keyBattles.title: Taremi vs Egypt's centre-backs
keyBattles.blurb: The marquee duel. Iran's everything — focal point in open play AND on set pieces, but largely isolated. Watch him drop to drag a CB out; that gap is Iran's best route in.

keyBattles.title: Egypt's double pivot vs Iran's counter-runners
keyBattles.blurb: The control battle. Egypt dominate the ball; the instant they lose it, Iran spring Ghoddos & Jahanbakhsh into the space the full-backs vacate. Snuff the first counter pass and Iran starve.

keyBattles.title: Marmoush's pace vs a 30-something back line
keyBattles.blurb: Can veteran defenders handle runners in behind for 90 minutes? Late game is where this opens up.

setPieces.egypt: Salah is the dead-ball weapon (direct FKs, corners, penalties); Marmoush/Zizo on delivery. Danger is delivery quality + Salah's boot more than a towering target.
setPieces.iran: A clear scoring route. Aerial targets Kanaani & Khalilzadeh plus Taremi attack corners/wide FKs (taken by Ghoddos, Taremi, Hosseinzadeh).
setPieces.fanTip: If it's 0-0 near the hour, treat every Iranian corner or wide free kick as a genuine chance — their most realistic path to a goal.

predictions.goals: Every desk leans OVER (1.5-2.5). Iran MUST win, forcing Ghalenoei out of his low block. BTTS lean YES.
predictions.predictedScore: Egypt 2-1 best estimate; 1-1 strong second (and the result that suits Egypt's math, so they may game-manage). Tail: 1-0 / 0-0.
predictions.rankingTwist: Iran is actually higher-ranked (FIFA 20 vs 28), yet Egypt are favorites on group position, form and star quality.

venue.name: Lumen Field (FIFA: 'Seattle Stadium')
venue.noise: A 200,000 sq-ft canopy covers ~70% of seats but leaves the field open — engineered as a 'natural megaphone'. FORMER loudest-stadium record holder (137.6 dB vs Saints, 2013); Arrowhead now leads at 142.2.
venue.the12s: Jersey #12 retired in 1984 to honor the fans; a flag is raised pre-match.
venue.wcRole: Hosts 6 World Cup matches incl. a Round of 32 and Round of 16.

funFacts: The 92-year wait: Egypt's 3-1 win over NZ (Jun 21) was their FIRST-EVER WC victory — 92 years and 25 days after their 1934 debut.
Egypt entered 2026 with a 0-win WC record (7 matches, 0W-2D-5L).
First-ever COMPETITIVE meeting between the two nations — and Egypt has never beaten Iran in regulation.
Iran has been eliminated in the group stage at all 7 of its previous World Cups.
Neither nation has EVER reached a World Cup knockout round — whoever advances tonight makes history.
Egypt scored the first-ever World Cup goal by an African (Fawzi's brace vs Hungary, 1934) — then waited generations for company.
Belgium, the group heavyweight, could be eliminated from a group Egypt and Iran survive — an upside-down Group G.
Two great goalkeeping footnotes meet: El-Hadary (oldest WC player ever, 45, in 2018) and Beiranvand (saved Ronaldo's penalty).
Salah chases his own coach: Hossam Hassan holds Egypt's 69-goal record; Salah is on 68.

storylines.title: Salah vs his own manager's record
storylines.blurb: Coach Hossam Hassan IS the 69-goal record-holder Salah (68) is chasing — on Hassan's own bench. A goal tonight equals it.

storylines.title: Egypt's first knockout berth in 92 years
storylines.blurb: First Arab/African nation at a World Cup (1934); never advanced. A draw makes history.

storylines.title: Iran's geopolitical ordeal
storylines.blurb: Based in Tijuana; visas ~10 days before the opener, ~15 staff denied entry, a 'matchday-minus-one' US travel rule, and a FIFA complaint. Torabi's visa expired after game one (later reissued).

storylines.title: Hajsafi chasing the cap record
storylines.blurb: On 148 — tonight equals Nekounam's all-time Iran record of 149, in his fourth World Cup as captain.

storylines.title: Beiranvand's redemption arc
storylines.blurb: The keeper who denied Ronaldo in 2018 was MOTM vs Belgium with 7 saves.

offPitch.iranTravel: Based & training in Tijuana, Mexico (moved from a planned Arizona/Tucson camp amid US visa problems). May enter the US only ~24h before a match and must leave right after — declined easing even for these games. Federation filed a FIFA complaint citing discrimination.
offPitch.diaspora: Southern California hosts the largest Iranian community outside Iran ('Tehrangeles'); the June 15 LA opener drew thousands of Iranian-American fans plus several hundred protesters. Seattle-specific turnout: unverified.
